run_type: architecture + forensic design — no local run (arcengine not importable outside Kaggle sandbox)

new_fields: pixel_diff (changed_pixels, changed_frac, added_pixels, removed_pixels, net_change, total_pixels)

ACTION_ID_UNKNOWN.trigger: every int ID in available_actions that cannot be mapped via GameAction.from_id()

P0_win_levels.problem: v11.0 tracked levels_completed from FrameData.levels_completed. The engine also provides win_levels (FrameData field) which is the authoritative win counter.
P0_win_levels.fix: v12.0 reads both levels_completed and win_levels, takes max(), and tracks _win_levels independently. Level-up detected if either increments.
P0_win_levels.evidence: FrameData.win_levels field confirmed present (arcengine/enums.py line 136: win_levels: int = Field(0, ge=0, le=254))

P0_action_ids.problem: GameAction enum has IDs 0-7 only. FrameData.available_actions is list[int]. If a game provides IDs like [22, 123, 73, 84, 96, 192, 186], GameAction.from_id() raises ValueError and they are silently ignored. LuCY falls back to ACTION1..ACTION7 — a subset that may never win.
P0_action_ids.fix: v12.0 audits all raw IDs, logs ACTION_ID_UNKNOWN events, and reports action_id_audit in GAME_DONE. Operator can now see exactly which games use out-of-range IDs.
P0_action_ids.evidence: arcengine/enums.py GameAction.from_id() line 89-93: raises ValueError for unknown ID. FrameData.available_actions: list[int] = [] (line 140).
P0_action_ids.implication: If all games use IDs > 7, LuCY is always using fallback actions and cannot win regardless of cognitive strategy. This must be confirmed by reading FRAME_INVENTORY logs.

P0_perception.problem: IDENTITY classification triggers when active_count, dominant_colour, and centre_of_mass are all equal. This is a coarse test — the pixel grid can change significantly while these three aggregates stay identical (e.g. a colour substitution with same count, same dominant, same CoM).
P0_perception.fix: v12.0 computes _pixel_diff_detail() for every action: changed_pixels, changed_frac, added_pixels, removed_pixels, net_change. Logged in ACTION_AFTER. This allows post-hoc detection of changes invisible to v11 classifiers.
P0_perception.note: _RuleMemory._classify() still uses the aggregate features — pixel_diff is forensic only in v12. A v13 improvement would be to feed pixel_diff back into classification.

P1_goal_delta.problem: LuCY had no access to the puzzle goal state. It was acting blindly, optimising for change (GROWING) rather than progress towards the target.
P1_goal_delta.fix: v12.0 _GoalDeltaTracker inspects FrameData for goal/target/answer/output_grid/expected_output/solution attributes. If found, computes goal_delta = fraction of pixels differing from goal. Feeds goal_delta_improvement into CognitiveEngine as W_GOAL_DELTA=5.0 signal.
P1_goal_delta.current_status: FRAME_INVENTORY will reveal whether any goal attribute exists in the live FrameData. If goal_found=false, this module is dormant and no performance change expected.
P1_goal_delta.verified_as_of: NOT_VERIFIED — requires live Kaggle run to confirm FrameData attrs

open_questions.Q1: Do any FrameData attrs contain a goal/target grid? Answer in FRAME_INVENTORY.goal_related_attrs after Kaggle run.
open_questions.Q2: Are baseline_actions [22,123,73,84,96,192,186] consistently available? Answer in ACTION_ID_AUDIT logs.
open_questions.Q3: Does win_levels ever increment? Or is levels_completed the correct counter? Answer after first run with a level win.
open_questions.Q4: What is the pixel_diff.changed_frac distribution? If all actions give changed_frac=0.000, the frame is truly static and IDENTITY is correct.
open_questions.Q5: What are the full FrameData available_actions int lists for the 25 test games? Needed to understand the action space.
